A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LVBench, and their text, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v2 ends with references and has no appendix; v3 includes readable Datasheet and capability-combination appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original model and human evaluations, an LLM-filtering ablation, answer-distribution analysis, and performance by video and clue duration.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark evaluations and reports additional model results, a frame-density ablation, and analysis of capability combinations.

M1.justification: The manual four-option annotation and GLM-4/GPT-4 agreement-based filtering remain unchanged. v3 expands the construction and annotation descriptions without establishing a new algorithm, model, or filtering procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same LVBench collection of 103 videos and 1,549 questions, covering six video categories and six composable capabilities. Appendix B analyzes existing capability combinations. The frame-count controls vary inputs within the retained task rather than adding dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands from 15 to 27 model entries, adding models including Qwen2.5-VL, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Seed1.5-VL, AdaReTaKe and MR.Video, and updates GPT-4o to a dated snapshot. Table 3 replaces InternVL2-40B and Qwen2-VL-72B with Seed1.5-VL and Gemini-2.5-Pro while retaining humans. The answer-distribution comparison also drops InternVL2-40B.

E3.justification: The main multiple-choice prompt, fixed-frame sampling and native-model 1 FPS handling are retained. v3 adds an auxiliary protocol testing three models with 0, 1, 4, 8, 50 frames and 1 FPS. The earlier filtered/unfiltered and duration-bin comparisons are removed, while the central benchmark evaluation protocol remains stable.

E4.justification: v2's filtering ablation (Table 4) and video/clue-duration analysis (Figure 5) are removed. v3 introduces a frame-density study with a zero-visual-input control (Section 4.5, Figure 4), addressing dependence on visual information. Appendix B adds the distribution of 26 capability combinations, and the retained failure analysis loses its InternVL2 comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 now has Gemini-2.5-Pro leading at 67.4%, while Qwen2-VL-72B retains 41.3%, reflecting expanded comparator coverage. The GLM4V-Plus overall score changes from 38.3% to 48.7%, and InternVL2-40B from 39.8% to 39.6%. Table 3 replaces model-specific category results while retaining human accuracy of 94.4%. Frame-count and capability-combination results are added; filtering and duration-stratified results are removed.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. Expanded descriptions of skills, events and clue durations do not introduce mathematical definitions, assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion preserve the benchmark contribution and the claim that current models fall short of human long-video understanding. The introduction retains the same contributions: six composable capabilities, unusually long and diverse videos, and controlled human annotation.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting dense frame input to temporal understanding and near-chance zero-frame performance to visual dependence. It explains entity/event label imbalance and replaces the image-to-video instruction-transfer hypothesis with insufficient long-video instruction data. Earlier filtering and clue-duration interpretations disappear. The datasheet adds annotator-bias and video-availability qualifications; the audio limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents 720p and event-density criteria, clue timestamp annotation, metadata fields, annotator compensation, licensing, and archival/removal policies. These are documentation additions, not evidence of reconstructed data. Conversely, it removes the project URL and changes the specified GLM-4 answer-extraction fallback to an unspecified LLM. Several datasheet access and maintenance fields remain anonymous placeholders.

R1.justification: The literature coverage adds contemporary models and methods, including Video-LLaMA, Qwen2.5-VL, Gemini 2.5, Seed1.5-VL, AdaReTaKe and MR.Video, while removing VideoChat and ST-LLM references. The model discussion emphasizes long-context architectures, but LVBench's broad positioning against shorter-video benchmarks remains intact.

P1.justification: The introduction, model-related-work discussion, dataset collection and question-generation sections are extensively rewritten. Annotation is organized into three named stages, experimental subsections are reorganized, and structured appendices are introduced. Author information and citation style also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from one-column to two-column layout. The opening category/radar overview, filtering table and duration plots are removed. Table 2 expands substantially; example labels and answer-distribution displays are revised; frame-density and capability-combination plots are added. Retained figures and tables are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The frame-density and zero-visual-input controls strengthen evidence for visual dependence, while expanded annotation, metadata and licensing documentation improves transparency. Updated model comparisons provide a more informative assessment of benchmark difficulty. These gains are limited by removal of useful filtering/duration diagnostics and the project link, plus unresolved anonymous datasheet fields. The net improvement is useful but modest.
